paragraphs: We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing treatments for inflammatory diseases, with an initial focus on severe respiratory disorders. We are developing verekitug, the only known antagonist currently in clinical development that targets the receptor for Thymic Stromal Lymphopoietin ("TSLP"), a cytokine which is a clinically validated driver of inflammatory response positioned upstream of multiple signaling cascades that affect a variety of immune mediated diseases. Preclinical and clinical data to date demonstrate verekitug's highly potent inhibition of the TSLP receptor, which we believe will translate to a differentiated product profile, including improved clinical outcomes, substantially extended dosing intervals and the potential to treat a broad spectrum of patients. We have advanced this highly potent monoclonal antibody into separate Phase 2 trials for the treatment of severe asthma, including a long-term safety and efficacy extension study ("Phase 2 LTE"), chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps ("CRSwNP"), and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease ("COPD"). We reported positive top-line results in our CRSwNP Phase 2 trial in September 2025 and positive top-line results in our severe asthma Phase 2 trial in February 2026. We initiated our Phase 2 COPD trial in July 2025. We plan to initiate dosing in Phase 3 trials in both severe asthma and CRSwNP in the first quarter of 2027, prioritizing a Phase 3 development strategy that focuses on maximizing efficacy in both indications, without biomarker restriction, with quarterly at-home administration. Our experienced team is committed to maximizing verekitug's unique attributes to address the substantial unmet needs for patients underserved by today's standard of care.

There are seven biologics approved for the treatment of severe asthma; four of these biologics are also approved for CRSwNP, and two are also approved for the treatment of COPD. Total estimated biologics sales in 2023 for asthma in the United States, Europe and Japan markets were approximately $7.5 billion. In December 2021, tezepelumab (marketed as Tezspire by Amgen Inc. ("Amgen") and AstraZeneca PLC ("AstraZeneca")), a monoclonal antibody targeting the TSLP ligand, not the receptor, was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") as an add-on maintenance treatment for patients with severe asthma. Tezepelumab is the first and only treatment for severe asthma without any phenotype or biomarker limitation, highlighting the benefit of blocking TSLP signaling early in the inflammatory cascade as compared to other biologics' mechanisms of action which are further downstream. Tezepelumab is projected to reach global annual sales of over $3.0 billion for severe asthma alone in 2032 and, according to Amgen, achieved more than 20% of new to brand share of prescriptions in the United States in its first commercial year. In May 2024, Amgen and AstraZeneca reported Phase 2a proof-of-concept data for tezepelumab for the treatment of moderate to very severe COPD at the American Thoracic Society ("ATS") International Conference. This trial reported a reduction in the frequency of COPD exacerbations that has supported advancement of tezepelumab into Phase 3 development for COPD. These clinical data further demonstrate the potential for a TSLP targeted therapy to treat a variety of inflammatory diseases. Tezepelumab is projected to reach global annual sales of over $5.0 billion for COPD alone in 2033, if approved in this indication. The projections for tezepelumab's global annual sales are not indicative of the potential market opportunity for verekitug and are subject to a number of assumptions, risks and uncertainties that could cause them to be smaller than currently estimated. Despite the availability of existing biologics for severe respiratory disease, there remains a high unmet need that limits the utilization of these therapies, including suboptimal symptom control and frequent dosing intervals.

Verekitug is, to our knowledge, the only monoclonal antibody currently in clinical development that targets and inhibits the TSLP receptor. In May 2024, we presented full proof-of-concept data from our multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1b multiple ascending dose ("MAD") clinical trial in asthma patients demonstrating that dosing with verekitug led to rapid and complete TSLP receptor occupancy, and reductions in fractional exhaled nitric oxide ("FeNO," a disease-related biomarker) and blood eosinophil levels ("eos," a disease-related biomarker) that were rapid, substantial and sustained for up to 24 weeks after the last dose. This study also demonstrated that verekitug is approximately 300-fold more potent than tezepelumab (based on published tezepelumab data), which, combined with verekitug's pharmacokinetic ("PK") profile, enables an extended dosing interval of up to 24 weeks, compared to tezepelumab (four-week dosing interval). Furthermore, clinical data from our MAD trial indicate an approximately 50% greater effect on FeNO than has previously been reported for tezepelumab. We have not conducted head-to-head clinical studies of verekitug against tezepelumab, and note that ongoing and future clinical trials for verekitug may produce differing clinical activity and tolerability results. Three Phase 1 clinical trials have been completed for verekitug across a total of 120 participants, including 32 patients with asthma. In these trials, which were not designed to support formal statistical comparisons, verekitug was well tolerated, demonstrated no evidence of clinically meaningful anti-drug antibodies ("ADAs"), and showed a predictable and consistent PK profile with high subcutaneous bioavailability. In December 2025, the full manuscript from the MAD trial was published in Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics. Based on its extended dosing interval and effect on broadly accepted disease-associated biomarkers, we believe verekitug, if approved, will be the preferred biologic for the treatment of severe asthma, CRSwNP and COPD.

Our current clinical development pipeline for verekitug is summarized in the chart below. We conducted two separate multi-national, placebo-controlled, randomized Phase 2 clinical trials to investigate the efficacy of two extended dosing intervals of 12 and 24 weeks for patients with severe asthma and 12 weeks for patients with CRSwNP. These trials were designed using endpoints that, pending interactions with regulatory authorities, could allow data from these trials to support submissions for product approval. We announced data from the Phase 2 clinical trial in CRSwNP in September 2025 and data from the Phase 2 clinical trial in severe asthma in February 2026. We plan to initiate dosing in Phase 3 trials in both severe asthma and CRSwNP in the first quarter of 2027, prioritizing a Phase 3 development strategy that focuses on maximizing efficacy in both indications, without biomarker restriction, with quarterly at-home administration. Based on available data from Phase 1 clinical trials with verekitug, we initiated our Phase 2 clinical trial in COPD in July 2025. Beyond these indications, we believe verekitug has broad potential, and we intend to leverage its unique attributes to develop it as a potential therapy for numerous TSLP-driven diseases.

Verekitug is a monoclonal antibody that targets and inhibits the TSLP receptor. TSLP is a member of a class of epithelial cytokines, also including IL-25 and IL-33, commonly referred to as alarmins. TSLP is primarily produced by epithelial cells, especially in the lung, gastrointestinal tract and skin. Dendritic cells, basophils, mast cells, keratinocytes and fibroblasts also produce TSLP with appropriate stimulation. In response to various environmental triggers, including viruses, bacteria, allergens, chemical irritants and physical injury, TSLP can initiate and amplify a wide range of innate and adaptive immune responses, including supporting epithelial barrier function, dendritic cell activation, type 2 innate lymphoid cell activation and survival, immune cell recruitment, induction of type 2 responses and regulation of B cell function. Beyond type 2 inflammation, data also support a role for TSLP in propagating non-type 2 inflammatory processes, including IL-17 production, modulation of airway structural cells and the promotion of fibrosis. As such, TSLP signaling is a central instigator of multiple downstream biologic pathways relevant to human diseases that are characterized by epithelial inflammation, including asthma, CRSwNP and COPD.

The TSLP signaling pathway is well-understood as a contributor to disease-driving proinflammatory pathways and is a clinically and commercially validated target for therapeutic development. Historically, development of biologics for severe asthma and related conditions has focused on type 2 inflammatory cytokines that are activated downstream in the TSLP signaling pathway, for instance IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13. However, in addition to its effect on type 2 inflammation, emerging evidence indicates that TSLP also impacts non-type 2 inflammation, which may result in broader downregulation of pathways relevant to the pathogenesis of multiple inflammatory diseases. We believe verekitug has the potential, if approved, to address unmet needs in multiple diseases characterized by TSLP-driven pathobiology due to the high potency and potential for extended dosing intervals that we have observed in our preclinical and clinical development to date.

Only one drug targeting the TSLP pathway has been approved for the treatment of severe asthma. In December 2021, tezepelumab (marketed as Tezspire by Amgen and AstraZeneca), a monoclonal antibody targeting the TSLP ligand, not the

receptor, was approved by the FDA as an add-on maintenance treatment for patients with severe asthma. Tezepelumab is the first and only treatment for severe asthma without any phenotype or biomarker limitation, highlighting the benefit of blocking TSLP signaling early in the inflammatory cascade as compared to other biologics' mechanisms of action which are further downstream. In the Phase 3 clinical trial of tezepelumab in adults and adolescents with severe, uncontrolled asthma, patients who received tezepelumab had fewer exacerbations and better lung function, asthma control and health-related quality of life than those who received placebo. Based on pooled safety data from the clinical trials of tezepelumab, Tezspire's FDA approved label identifies hypersensitivity reactions following administration as a clinically significant adverse reaction, as well as pharyngitis, arthralgia and back pain as additional adverse reactions that occurred at an incidence of greater than or equal to 3% and more common than the placebo group. Furthermore, a Phase 2a clinical trial for tezepelumab in COPD patients, which demonstrated a clinically-significant reduction of COPD exacerbations, the most frequently reported adverse events for tezepelumab were worsening of COPD (12.1%) and incidents of COVID-19 infections (14.5%, trial commenced in July 2019), demonstrating a safety and tolerability profile consistent with that observed for tezepelumab in severe asthma. In October 2025, tezepelumab was approved in the U.S. for the add-on maintenance treatment of adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with inadequately controlled CRSwNP. This approval was based on the efficacy and safety data from its Phase 3 trial; in this study, tezepelumab demonstrated a reduction in nasal polyp severity and showed reduction for the need for surgery and systemic corticosteroid use versus placebo. These clinical data further demonstrate the potential for a TSLP targeted therapy to treat a variety of inflammatory diseases.

Asthma is a common respiratory disease characterized by chronic airway inflammation that is often underdiagnosed and under-treated. For some people, asthma can simply be a nuisance, for others it can interfere with daily life and potentially even be life-threatening. Of the more than 25 million Americans living with asthma, it is estimated that 5% to 10% suffer from severe asthma. Severe asthma is defined as asthma that remains uncontrolled despite optimized treatment with high-dose inhaled corticosteroids or that requires high-dosed inhaled corticosteroids to prevent symptoms from becoming uncontrolled. It is estimated that approximately 90% of people with severe asthma are eligible for biologics, but only 440,000 patients are currently treated with biologics, suggesting more than 80% of eligible patients are not being optimally treated. In 2023, global sales of biologics for the treatment of severe asthma were approximately $7.5 billion.

These statistics show there is a large population of people living with uncontrolled symptoms of severe asthma. Key areas of unmet need for people living with severe asthma include improved control of exacerbations and symptoms and reduced treatment burden (e.g., need for frequent injections).
Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP)

CRSwNP is an inflammatory disease of the upper airway, marked by chronic sinonasal inflammation and the presence of inflammatory polyps in the nasal passages and paranasal sinuses. It is estimated by Sanofi that approximately 900,000 patients in the United States and Europe suffer from CRSwNP. Nasal polyps are associated with significant morbidity and debilitating symptoms; it is estimated that more than 40% of people with severe asthma also have CRSwNP and that up to 70% of people with CRSwNP also have asthma, demonstrating a strong association between the two conditions.

The current treatment options for patients with CRSwNP are corticosteroids, surgery and, more recently, biologics. Although a treatment option, surgery does not guarantee symptom relief. Even with surgery, many people with CRSwNP remain symptomatic, with the recurrence rate of CRSwNP ranging from 20% to 60% within 18 months to four years and increasing to 79% after 12 years. Recurrence is particularly common for people with severe disease, including those also living with asthma or who have undergone prior surgeries. The recent FDA approvals of biologic treatments for CRSwNP have established a well-understood regulatory pathway and route to commercialization. It is estimated that approximately 300,000 adult patients in the United States are eligible for biologics.

Despite these available treatments, the quality of life ("QoL") studies and post-surgical recurrence rates clearly show that many people with CRSwNP have uncontrolled symptoms that are impacting their daily life and current treatments are not meeting their needs.

We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company with a limited operating history. We were formed in April 2021 and our operations to date have been limited to pre-commercial activities. We have not yet demonstrated an ability to generate revenues, obtain regulatory approvals, manufacture any product on a commercial scale or arrange for a third party to do so on our behalf or conduct sales and marketing activities necessary for successful product commercialization. Our limited operating history as a company makes any assessment of our future success and viability subject to significant uncertainty. We will encounter risks and difficulties frequently experienced by early-stage biopharmaceutical companies in rapidly evolving fields, and we have not yet
demonstrated an ability to successfully overcome such risks and difficulties. If we do not address these risks and difficulties successfully, our business will suffer.

We have no products approved for commercial sale and have not generated any revenue from product sales to date. Verekitug is currently our only product candidate. We will continue to incur significant research and development and other expenses related to our preclinical and clinical development of verekitug and ongoing operations. As a result, we are not profitable and have incurred losses in each period since our inception. Net losses and negative cash flows have had, and will continue to have, an adverse effect on our stockholders' equity and working capital. Our net losses totaled $143.4 million and $62.8 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $334.2 million. We expect to continue to incur significant losses for the foreseeable future, and we expect these losses to increase as we continue our research and development of, and seek regulatory approvals for, verekitug in multiple indications.

Since our inception, we have devoted substantially all of our resources to organizing and staffing our company, business planning, raising capital, establishing licensing, building our proprietary platform technologies, developing verekitug, establishing our intellectual property portfolio, conducting research, preclinical studies, and clinical trials, establishing arrangements with third parties for the manufacture of verekitug and related raw materials, and providing general and administrative support for these operations. To date, we have financed our operations primarily through the issuance and sale of our redeemable convertible preferred stock and proceeds from our initial public offering ("IPO"). As of December 31, 2025, we have received total gross proceeds of $400.0 million from the issuance and sale of our redeemable convertible preferred stock. In October 2024, we completed our IPO in which we issued and sold 17,250,000 shares of our common stock, including 2,250,000 shares pursuant to the full exercise of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares, at a price to the public of $17.00 per share. As a result of the IPO, we received $268.8 million in net proceeds, after deducting $20.5 million in underwriting discounts and commissions, and $3.9 million in other offering costs.

We have incurred significant net operating losses and negative cash flows since our inception. Our ability to generate product revenue sufficient to achieve profitability, if ever, will depend on the successful development, regulatory approval and eventual commercialization of verekitug and any other potential future product candidates, which we expect will take a number of years. For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we reported net losses of $143.4 million and $62.8 million, respectively. Our net losses have resulted principally from costs incurred in our research and development activities. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $334.2 million, and we had cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments of $341.5 million. Based on our current operating plan, we believe that our existing cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments will be sufficient to fund our operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements through 2027.
We expect to continue to incur significant net operating losses for the foreseeable future. We anticipate that our expenses will increase substantially if, and as we:

• continue to conduct our ongoing clinical trials of verekitug, including our global Phase 2 clinical trials, as well as initiate and complete additional clinical trials of verekitug in new indications or patient populations;
• conduct larger-scale clinical trials for verekitug or any potential future product candidates;
• manufacture, or have manufactured, clinical and commercial supplies of verekitug;
• seek regulatory approvals, prepare for and, if approved, proceed to commercialization for verekitug in current or new indications or any potential future product candidates;
• attract, hire and retain additional clinical, scientific, and management personnel; • implement operational, financial, and management information systems;
• add quality control, quality assurance, legal, compliance, and other groups to support our operations;
• obtain, maintain, protect, expand and enforce our intellectual property portfolio, including intellectual property obtained through license agreements;
• defend against any claims by third parties that we have infringed, misappropriated or otherwise violated any intellectual property of any such third party;
• make royalty, milestone or other payments under current, and any future, license or collaboration agreements;

paragraphs: 本公司為一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，致力於開發治療發炎性疾病的方法，初期重點為嚴重呼吸道疾病。本公司正在開發 verekitug，這是目前唯一已知的拮抗劑，正在進行臨牀開發，目標為 Thymic Stromal Lymphopoietin（"TSLP"）受體，TSLP 是一種臨牀已驗證的發炎反應驅動因子，位於多種訊號傳導 cascade 的上游，影響多種免疫相關疾病。截至目前為止的預臨牀與臨牀數據顯示 verekitug 對 TSLP 受體具有高度強效的抑制作用，本公司認為這將轉化為差異化的產品特性，包括改善臨牀結果、大幅延長給藥間隔，以及治療廣泛病患的潛力。本公司已將這高度強效的單株抗體推進至針對嚴重氣喘的分階段 2 試驗，包括長期安全性與有效性延續研究（"分階段 2 LTE"）、慢性鼻竇炎伴隨鼻息肉（"CRSwNP"）以及慢性阻塞性肺病（"COPD"）的分階段 2 試驗。本公司於 2025 年 9 月報告了 CRSwNP 分階段 2 試驗的正面初步結果，並於 2026 年 2 月報告了嚴重氣喘分階段 2 試驗的正面初步結果。本公司於 2025 年 7 月啟動了分階段 2 COPD 試驗。本公司計畫於 2027 年第一季啟動分階段 3 試驗，針對嚴重氣喘與 CRSwNP，優先採用分階段 3 開發策略，專注於最大化兩種適應症的療效，不以生物標記為限制，並以每季在家給藥的方式進行。本公司經驗豐富的團隊致力於最大化 verekitug 的獨特特性，以解決目前標準照護未被滿足的患者的重大需求。

目前有七種生物製劑已核准用於治療嚴重氣喘；其中四種也核准用於 CRSwNP，兩種也核准用於治療 COPD。2023 年美國、歐洲與日本市場的氣喘生物製劑銷售總額估計約為 7.5 十億美元。2021 年 12 月，tezepelumab（由 Amgen Inc.（"Amgen"）與 AstraZeneca PLC（"AstraZeneca"）行銷為 Tezspire）一種針對 TSLP 結合物而非受體的單株抗體，獲美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准作為嚴重氣喘患者的附加維持治療。Tezepelumab 是第一種且唯一一種不具任何表型或生物標記限制的嚴重氣喘治療藥物，突顯了在發炎 cascade 的早期阻斷 TSLP 信號的優勢，與其他生物製劑的機製作用相比，這些機製作用更在下游。Tezepelumab 預計在 2032 年單獨用於嚴重氣喘的全球年銷售額將超過 3.0 十億美元，根據 Amgen 的報告，其在第一年商業化時已達成超過 20% 的新品牌處方比例。2024 年 5 月，Amgen 與 AstraZeneca 在美國胸科學會（"ATS"）國際會議上報告了 tezepelumab 對中度至非常嚴重 COPD 治療的分階段 2a 概念驗證數據。此試驗報告了 COPD 情況惡化頻率的減少，支持 tezepelumab 進入 COPD 的分階段 3 開發。這些臨牀數據進一步顯示了針對 TSLP 的治療藥物治療多種發炎性疾病潛力。Tezepelumab 預計在 2033 年單獨用於 COPD 的全球年銷售額將超過 5.0 十億美元，若在該適應症核准。Tezepelumab 的全球年銷售額預測並不代表 verekitug 的潛在市場機會，且受到許多假設、風險與不確定因素的影響，這些因素可能導致預測結果小於目前的估計。儘管已有現有的生物製劑用於嚴重呼吸道疾病，但仍有高度未被滿足的需求，限制了這些治療藥物的使用，包括症狀控制不佳與頻繁的給藥間隔。

Verekitug，據本公司所知，是目前唯一正在進行臨牀開發的單株抗體，目標為並抑制 TSLP 受體。2024 年 5 月，本公司在哮喘患者的多中心、隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照的分階段 1b 多次遞增劑量（"MAD"）臨牀試驗中，展示了完整的概念驗證數據，顯示 verekitug 的給藥導致 TSLP 受體快速且完全佔據，並減少分數呼出一氧化氮（"FeNO"，一種疾病相關生物標記）和血液嗜酸性球（"eos"，一種疾病相關生物標記）的水平，這些變化快速、顯著且在最後一次給藥後持續達 24 週。此研究也顯示 verekitug 的強效程度約為 tezepelumab 的 300 倍（根據已發表的 tezepelumab 數據），結合 verekitug 的藥代動力學（"PK"）特性，使其給藥間隔可延長至 24 週，與 tezepelumab（四週給藥間隔）相比。此外，來自我們 MAD 試驗的臨牀數據顯示 verekitug 對 FeNO 的影響約為 tezepelumab 報告的 50% 更高。本公司尚未進行 verekitug 與 tezepelumab 的頭對頭臨牀試驗，並指出 ongoing 和未來的 verekitug 臨牀試驗可能產生不同的臨牀活動和耐受性結果。Verekitug 已完成三項分階段 1 臨牀試驗，總共 120 名參與者，包括 32 名氣喘患者。在這些試驗中，並未設計用以支持正式的統計比較，verekitug 被認為耐受良好，未顯示 clinically meaningful 的抗藥物抗體（"ADAs"），並顯示可預測且一致的 PK 特性與高皮下生物可用性。2025 年 12 月，MAD 試驗的完整論文在 Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics 發表。根據其延長的給藥間隔與對廣泛接受的疾病相關生物標記的影響，本公司認為 verekitug 若核准，將成為治療嚴重氣喘、CRSwNP 和 COPD 的首選生物製劑。

本公司目前 verekitug 的臨牀開發路線圖如下圖所示。本公司進行了兩項分離的多國、安慰劑對照、隨機分階段 2 臨牀試驗，以研究 12 週和 24 週的延長給藥間隔對嚴重氣喘患者和 12 週對 CRSwNP 患者的有效性。這些試驗設計使用了端點，待與監管當局互動後，可能允許這些試驗的數據支持產品核准的申請。本公司於 2025 年 9 月宣佈了 CRSwNP 分階段 2 臨牀試驗的數據，並於 2026 年 2 月宣佈了嚴重氣喘分階段 2 臨牀試驗的數據。本公司計畫於 2027 年第一季啟動分階段 3 臨牀試驗，針對嚴重氣喘與 CRSwNP，優先採用分階段 3 開發策略，專注於最大化兩種適應症的療效，不以生物標記為限制，並以每季在家給藥的方式進行。根據 verekitug 的分階段 1 臨牀試驗可用數據，本公司於 2025 年 7 月啟動了 COPD 的分階段 2 臨牀試驗。除了這些適應症之外，本公司認為 verekitug 有廣泛的潛力，並計畫利用其獨特特性，開發為多種 TSLP 驅動疾病的潛在治療藥物。

Verekitug 是一種單株抗體，針對並抑制 TSLP 受體。TSLP 是一種上皮細胞類激素，也包括 IL-25 和 IL-33，常被稱為 alarmins。TSLP 主要由上皮細胞產生，特別是在肺部、消化道和皮膚。樹狀細胞、嗜鹼性粒細胞、肥大細胞、角質細胞和纖維母細胞在適當刺激下也會產生 TSLP。面對各種環境觸發因素，包括病毒、細菌、過敏原、化學刺激物和物理傷害，TSLP 可以啟動並放大廣泛的先天與適應性免疫反應，包括支持上皮屏障功能、樹狀細胞活化、型 2 先天淋巴細胞活化與存活、免疫細胞招募、誘導型 2 反應以及調控 B 細胞功能。除了型 2 炎症，數據也支持 TSLP 在傳播非型 2 炎症過程中的作用，包括 IL-17 產生、氣道結構細胞調節以及促進纖維化。因此，TSLP 信號傳導是多種下游生物學途徑的中心驅動因素，這些途徑與人類疾病相關，這些疾病特徵為上皮炎症，包括氣喘、CRSwNP 和 COPD。

TSLP 信號傳導途徑已被廣泛了解為疾病驅動的促炎途徑的貢獻者，且是臨牀和商業上已驗證的治療開發目標。歷史上，針對嚴重氣喘及相關疾病的生物製劑開發，主要聚焦於 TSLP 信號傳導途徑下游活化的型 2 炎症細胞激素，例如 IL-4、IL-5 和 IL-13。然而，除了對型 2 炎症的影響，新興證據顯示 TSLP 也會影響非型 2 炎症，這可能導致與多種炎症疾病發病機制相關的途徑更廣泛的調節。我們認為，若 verekitug 被核准，它有潛力解決多種以 TSLP 驅動的病生理學特徵疾病未被滿足的需求，這是因為我們在目前的臨牀前及臨牀開發中觀察到的高強度及潛在延長給藥間隔的特性。
僅有一種針對 TSLP 途徑的藥物已獲批准用於治療嚴重哮喘。2021 年 12 月，tezepelumab（由 Amgen 和 AstraZeneca 推廣銷售，商品名為 Tezspire），一種針對 TSLP 綁定物的單株抗體，而非

receptor, 被美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准作為嚴重氣喘患者的附加維持治療。Tezepelumab 是目前唯一且唯一可用於治療嚴重氣喘，不論其表現型或生物標記限制的治療方式，突顯了在發炎 cascade 中早期阻斷 TSLP 信號的優勢，與其他生物製劑的機製作用相比，其作用點更為上游。在 Tezepelumab 對於成人及青少年嚴重且無法控制的氣喘的第三期臨牀試驗中，接受 Tezepelumab 治療的患者，其急性發作次數較少，肺功能、氣喘控制及健康相關的生活品質均優於接受安慰劑的患者。根據 Tezepelumab 臨牀試驗的總合安全性資料，Tezspire 的 FDA 核准標籤指出，注射後的過敏反應被視為臨牀上重要的不良反應，同時喉嚨炎、關節痛及背痛也被列為發生率高於或等於 3% 且比安慰劑組更常見的不良反應。此外，在 COPD 患者中進行的 Tezepelumab 第二期臨牀試驗顯示，COPD 急性發作有臨牀上顯著的減少，Tezepelumab 最常見的不良反應為 COPD 情況惡化（12.1%）及 COVID-19 感染事件（14.5%，試驗於 2019 年 7 月啟動），顯示其安全性與耐受性與 Tezepelumab 在嚴重氣喘中的觀察結果一致。2025 年 10 月，Tezepelumab 在美國獲准用於 12 歲以上且控制不佳的 CRSwNP 成人及兒童患者的附加維持治療。此核准基於其第三期試驗的療效與安全性資料；在該研究中，Tezepelumab 顯示出鼻息肉嚴重程度的減少，以及減少手術與系統性類固醇使用的需求，與安慰劑相比。這些臨牀資料進一步顯示出針對 TSLP 的治療方式在治療多種發炎性疾病方面的潛力。

氣喘是一種常見的呼吸系統疾病，特徵為慢性氣道發炎，常被低估且治療不足。對某些人來說，氣喘可能只是小麻煩，對其他人則可能影響日常生活，甚至危及生命。根據估計，美國有超過25百萬人患有氣喘，其中5%至10%患有嚴重氣喘。嚴重氣喘被定義為即使使用高劑量吸入性類固醇治療仍無法控制的氣喘，或需要高劑量吸入性類固醇來預防症狀失控的氣喘。估計約有90%的嚴重氣喘患者符合生物製劑治療資格，但目前僅有440,000名患者接受生物製劑治療，顯示超過80%的資格患者未獲得最佳治療。2023年，用於治療嚴重氣喘的生物製劑全球銷售額約為7.5十億美元。
這些統計數據顯示，有大量人口患有未控制的嚴重氣喘症狀。患有嚴重氣喘的人羣中，未滿足的關鍵需求包括改善發作和症狀的控制，以及減少治療負擔（例如需要頻繁注射）。
慢性鼻竇炎伴隨鼻息肉（CRSwNP）
CRSwNP是一種上呼吸道的發炎疾病，特徵為慢性鼻竇發炎以及鼻腔和顳顬竇中存在發炎性息肉。根據Sanofi的估計，美國和歐洲約有900,000名患者患有CRSwNP。鼻息肉與顯著的疾病負荷和令人無法忍受的症狀有關；估計超過40%的嚴重氣喘患者同時患有CRSwNP，且最多70%的CRSwNP患者同時患有氣喘，顯示這兩種疾病之間有強烈的關聯。

目前治療CRSwNP患者的治療選項包括類固醇、手術以及更近期的生物製劑。雖然手術是一種治療選項，但無法保證症狀緩解。即使進行手術，許多CRSwNP患者仍會有症狀，CRSwNP的復發率在18個月至四年間為20%至60%，並在12年後增加至79%。復發尤其常見於患有嚴重疾病的患者，包括同時患有氣喘或曾接受過手術的患者。近期美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准用於治療CRSwNP的生物製劑治療方案，已建立一個明確的監管途徑和商業化路線。估計美國約有300,000名成人患者符合生物製劑治療資格。
儘管有這些治療選項，品質生活（"QoL"）研究和手術後復發率清楚顯示，許多CRSwNP患者仍有未控制的症狀，影響其日常生活，且目前的治療方式未能滿足其需求。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，並與我們合併財務報表及相關附註及其他財務資訊一併參考，這些資訊包含於本年度報表（Form 10-K）中（簡稱「本年度報告」）。本討論與分析中部分資訊，或於本年度報告其他處所提及之資訊，包括有關我們業務計畫與策略之資訊，包含風險與不確定性之預測性陳述。您應審閱本年度報告「項目 1A、風險因素」，以瞭解可能導致實際結果與預測性陳述中所述或暗示之結果有重大差異的重要因素。請同時參閱本年度報告其他處所包含的「特別說明預測性陳述」部分。

我們是一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，專注於開發治療發炎性疾病之療法，初期重點為嚴重呼吸道疾病。我們正在開發 verekitug，這是目前唯一在臨牀開發階段的拮抗劑，目標為 Thymic Stromal Lymphopoietin（簡稱「TSLP」）受體，TSLP 是一種臨牀驗證過的發炎反應驅動因子，位於多種訊號傳導路徑上游，影響多種免疫相關疾病。截至目前為止的預臨牀與臨牀數據顯示 verekitug 對 TSLP 受體具有高度強效的抑制作用，我們相信這將轉化為差異化的產品特性，包括改善的臨牀結果、大幅延長給藥間隔，以及治療廣泛病患的潛力。我們已將這高度強效的單株抗體推進至針對嚴重氣喘的分階段 2 試驗，包括長期安全性與有效性延長研究（簡稱「分階段 2 LTE」）、慢性鼻竇炎伴鼻息肉（簡稱「CRSwNP」）以及慢性阻塞性肺病（簡稱「COPD」）的分階段 2 試驗。我們在 2025 年 9 月報告了 CRSwNP 分階段 2 試驗的正面初步結果，並在 2026 年 2 月報告了嚴重氣喘分階段 2 試驗的正面初步結果。我們在 2025 年 7 月啟動了 COPD 分階段 2 試驗。我們預計在 2027 年第一季啟動嚴重氣喘與 CRSwNP 的分階段 3 試驗，優先採用聚焦於最大化兩種適應症療效的分階段 3 發展策略，不以生物標記為限制，並以每季在家給藥方式進行。我們經驗豐富的團隊致力於最大化 verekitug 的獨特特性，以解決目前標準照護未充分照顧的患者的重大未滿足需求。

自成立以來，我們將幾乎所有資源投入於組織與僱用公司員工、業務計畫、籌資、建立授權、建立專屬平台技術、開發 verekitug、建立智慧財產權組合、進行研究、預臨牀研究、臨牀試驗、與第三方建立製造 verekitug 及相關原料的協議，以及提供這些運作的一般及行政支援。截至目前為止，我們主要透過發行與銷售可轉換優先股，以及首次公開發行（簡稱「IPO」）所得資金來支應運作。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們透過發行與銷售可轉換優先股已收到總計 400.0 百萬美元的淨資金。2024 年 10 月，我們完成 IPO，發行並銷售 17,250,000 股普通股，包括 2,250,000 股根據發行機構選擇權完全行使後的額外股份，發行價格為每股 17.00 美元。因 IPO 而獲得的淨資金為 268.8 百萬美元，扣除 20.5 百萬美元的發行機構折扣與佣金，以及 3.9 百萬美元的其他發行費用後計算。

自成立以來，我們已產生顯著的淨營運虧損與負現金流。我們能否產生足夠的產品收入以達到獲利，若有可能，將取決於 verekitug 及任何其他潛在未來產品候選藥物的成功開發、監管批准與最終商業化，而我們預期這將需要數年時間。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日，我們分別報告淨虧損為 143.4 百萬美元與 62.8 百萬美元。我們的淨虧損主要來自研究與開發活動的費用。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們累積虧損為 334.2 百萬美元，且我們擁有現金、現金等價物及短期投資 341.5 百萬美元。根據我們目前的運作計畫，我們相信現有的現金及現金等價物與短期投資將足以支應至 2027 年的運作費用與資本支出需求。
我們預期將持續產生顯著的淨營運虧損，至少在可預見的未來。我們預期，若我們：
• 繼續進行 verekitug 的臨牀試驗，包括全球分階段 2 臨牀試驗，以及啟動並完成 verekitug 在新適應症或病患羣體的臨牀試驗；
• 進行 verekitug 或任何潛在未來產品候選藥物的更大規模臨牀試驗；
• 生產，或委託生產，verekitug 的臨牀與商業用供應；
• 申請相關主管機關審批，並為 verekitug 在現有或新適應症或任何潛在未來產品候選藥物進行商業化做準備，若獲批准則進行商業化;
• 吸引、僱用並留住更多臨牀、科學及管理人員；• 落實營運、財務及管理資訊系統;
• 增設品質控制、品質保證、法律、合規及其他部門以支援本公司營運;
• 取得、維持、保護、擴充並執行本公司智慧財產權組合，包括透過授權協議取得的智慧財產權;
• 回應任何第三方提出的聲請，聲稱本公司侵權、竊取或以其他方式違反該第三方之智慧財產權;
• 根據現有及未來之授權或合作協議，支付版稅、里程碑或其他費用;

headings: 與本公司有限的營運歷史、財務狀況及對額外資金需求相關之風險
籌措額外資金可能導致股東持股稀釋、限制本公司營運或要求本公司放棄對 verekitug 或任何其他潛在未來產品候選藥物之權利。
與本公司業務相關之風險
verekitug 為本公司唯一產品候選藥物，且本公司依賴第三方準確產生、收集及報告曾為 verekitug 進行之某些臨牀前研究資料。
藥物產品之成功開發涉及漫長且昂貴的過程，且具有高度不確定性。
某些市場潛力之估計及預測可能低於本公司所預期。
若本公司成功商業化 verekitug，本公司營運成果將受本公司需支付給 Regeneron 之版稅金額影響。
人工智慧帶來風險與挑戰，可能影響本公司業務，包括對本公司機密資訊、專有資訊及個人資料造成安全風險。

paragraphs: 本公司業務涉及重大風險。投資人應謹慎考量下列所描述的風險與不確定性，以及本年度報告表10-K（本「年度報告」）與其他提交至證券交易委員會（「SEC」）的文件中所包含的其他資訊。下列所描述的風險並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。上述風險，或目前未知的其他風險與不確定性，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果與成長前景造成重大且不利的影響。在這種情況下，本公司普通股的交易價格可能下跌，投資人可能損失全部或部分投資。
本年度報告亦包含涉及風險與不確定性的展望性陳述與預估，這些風險與不確定性目前未知或本公司認為不重要。這些也可能影響本公司營運。請參閱本年度報告中其他處的「特別注意展望性陳述」以取得更多資訊。本公司實際結果可能與展望性陳述中預期的結果有重大差異，原因包括下列所描述的風險與不確定性。
本公司為一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，營運歷史有限，這可能使評估本公司目前業務與預測未來成功與生存能力變得困難。自本公司成立以來，我們已產生重大財務虧損，並預期在可預見的未來持續產生重大財務虧損。
本公司為一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，營運歷史有限。本公司於2021年4月成立，截至目前為止的營運活動僅限於預商業活動。我們尚未展示出產生收入、取得監管批准、大規模製造任何產品或委託第三方代為製造，或進行成功產品商業化所需的銷售與行銷活動的能力。本公司營運歷史有限，使對本公司未來成功與生存能力的評估面臨重大不確定性。我們將經常面臨早期階段生物科技公司於快速變遷領域中常見的風險與困難，而我們尚未
展示出成功克服這些風險與困難的能力。若我們未能成功解決這些風險與困難，將對本公司業務造成不利影響。

本公司目前尚無產品獲得商業銷售許可，且至今尚未從產品銷售中產生任何營業收入。Verekitug 現為本公司唯一產品候選品。本公司將持續產生與 verekitug 的臨牀前及臨牀開發以及持續運作相關的重大研究與開發及其他費用。因此，本公司尚未實現盈利，且自成立以來每個會計期間均產生虧損。淨虧損及負面現金流已對本公司股東權益及營運資金產生不利影響，並將持續產生此等影響。本公司於 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度之淨虧損為 143.4 百萬美元，2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度之淨虧損為 62.8 百萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司累計虧損為 334.2 百萬美元。本公司預期將持續產生重大虧損，且隨著本公司持續進行 verekitug 的研究與開發，並尋求多個適應症之監管批准，這些虧損將進一步增加。
